title: An Eye-Opening Arbiter PUF for Fingerprint Generation Using Auto-Error Detection for PVT-Robust Masking and Bit Stabilization Achieving a BER of 2e-8 in 28nm CMOS
problem: Physically unclonable functions (PUFs) for hardware identification and key generation must maintain constant fingerprint across voltage, temperature, and time variations while minimizing bit error rate (BER), but prior techniques either sacrifice speed/area for low BER via averaging/masking or rely on shared/off-chip error-correction hardware with security risks.
motivation: Secure hardware identification and key generation require on-chip, PVT-robust PUFs without area-expensive error-correction codes.
method: The circuit uses a race between two electrical signals—an arbiter—to detect tiny manufacturing variations in the silicon, creating a unique fingerprint for each chip. It includes built-in error detection that identifies unstable bit readings when voltage, temperature, or the chip ages over time (variations known as PVT changes), and automatically corrects those bits to keep the fingerprint steady. This on-chip correction achieves an extremely low error rate of just 2 in 100 million readings using 28nm-size transistors, without requiring large external error-correction hardware.
key_novelty: Automatic error detection built into the chip allows it to stabilize the fingerprint across voltage and temperature changes without needing external error-correction hardware.
contributions: Arbiter PUF achieving BER of 2e-8 (extremely low, minimal error correction needed)
Auto-error-detection enabling on-chip masking without large dedicated hardware
PVT robustness across voltage, temperature, and aging variations
baselines: delay-based arbiter PUFs with shared/off-chip error correction
limitations: Fingerprint entropy, readout speed, and area trade-offs with prior designs not provided.
primary_theme: Low-BER arbiter PUF with on-chip error detection.
